cases.purpose: --hctosys --localtime under EST5EDT,M3.2.0/2,M11.1.0/2 converts ordinary local calendars (summer, winter, just after the spring gap, around the fall fold) to the independent epoch and issues one CLOCK_REALTIME set
cases.oracle: Independently derived epochs (UTC instants of the local calendars under the US rule EST5EDT,M3.2.0/2,M11.1.0/2 from Gregorian arithmetic, checked against zoneinfo America/New_York) and a synthetic RTC/clock recorder (helpers/mig-w6-hwclock-synth.py); no real RTC or clock is touched
cases.comparison: The recorded clock_settime seconds for five local RTC calendars against independent epochs.
cases.script:
[[ $UID == 2000 && $EUID == 2000 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r marker </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125
IFS= read -r vendor </sys/class/dmi/id/sys_vendor || exit 125
[[ $vendor == QEMU && $marker =~ ^[0-9a-fA-F]{8}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{4}-[0-9a-fA-F]{12}$ ]] || exit 125
[[ $(type -t hwclock) == builtin ]] || exit 125
: >rtc
HS=/opt/bashos-parity/harness/helpers/mig-w6-hwclock-synth.py
export TZ='EST5EDT,M3.2.0/2,M11.1.0/2'
# hs LABEL RTC-JSON-ARRAY PROBE-TEXT COMMAND-OPTIONS
hs() {
  printf '{"rtc": %s}\n' "$2" >synth.json
  local out err rc
  out=$(/usr/bin/python3 "$HS" "$BASH" --noprofile --norc -c "hwclock $4 --noadjfile --rtc /tmp/parity-case/rtc 2>\"\$HOME/op.err\"; echo \$? >\"\$HOME/op.rc\"")
  rc=$(<"$HOME/op.rc"); err=$(<"$HOME/op.err")
  HSOUT=$out
  local p=''; [[ -n $3 ]] && p=" probe=$([[ $err == *"$3"* ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
  echo "$1: rc=$rc [${out//$'\n'/ ; }]$p"
}
hs jul "[0,0,12,4,6,124,0,0,0]" "" "--hctosys --localtime"
hs jan "[0,30,8,15,0,124,0,0,0]" "" "--hctosys --localtime"
hs after-gap "[0,0,3,10,2,124,0,0,0]" "" "--hctosys --localtime"
hs before-fold "[59,59,0,3,10,124,0,0,0]" "" "--hctosys --localtime"
hs after-fold "[0,0,2,3,10,124,0,0,0]" "" "--hctosys --localtime"
cases.stdout:
jul: rc=0 [rd ; clock_settime clk=0 sec=1720108800 nsec=0]
jan: rc=0 [rd ; clock_settime clk=0 sec=1705325400 nsec=0]
after-gap: rc=0 [rd ; clock_settime clk=0 sec=1710054000 nsec=0]
before-fold: rc=0 [rd ; clock_settime clk=0 sec=1730609999 nsec=0]
after-fold: rc=0 [rd ; clock_settime clk=0 sec=1730617200 nsec=0]

cases.purpose: For the repeated local hour 2024-11-03 01:30:00 the result is one of the two valid epochs (1730611800 EDT, 1730615400 EST) and equals libc mktime with tm_isdst=-1

cases.comparison: Membership of the recorded epoch in the two valid values and equality with mktime. Obtaining the other epoch is not asserted (no fold selector exists).

cases.purpose: --systohc converts a FIXED system time (CLOCK_REALTIME set by root to 2024-06-15 12:34:50 UTC) to RTC fields, UTC and local (EST5EDT), and issues one RTC_SET_TIME
cases.oracle: Fixed instant set by root and independent calendar arithmetic (UTC 12:34:50; EDT local 08:34:50); the RTC is a synthetic recorder
cases.comparison: The six RTC_SET_TIME fields recorded for --utc and --localtime; the seconds field is within a 3 s window after the fixed instant.
cases.script:
[[ $UID == 0 && $EUID == 0 && $PWD == /tmp/parity-case && $HOME == /tmp/parity-home ]] || exit 125
IFS= read -r marker </etc/bashos-parity-vm || exit 125

/usr/bin/date -u -s '2024-06-15 12:34:50' >/dev/null || exit 97

ev=${HSOUT##*set }; IFS=, read -r s mi h d mo y <<<"$ev"
echo "utc: min=$mi hour=$h mday=$d mon=$mo year=$y sec-in-window=$([[ $s -ge 50 && $s -le 53 ]] && echo 1 || echo 0)"
